Messages.Author: Gomi no Sensei
Messages.Body:
In article <757h98$b...@sjx-ixn3.ix.netcom.com>,
Randi S. Herdman <ran...@ix.netcom.com> wrote:

>Can non-preventable aggravated damage (i.e., dawn operation with weather
>control, force of will,
>or daring the dawn) be changed to regular damage using skin of night?

Force of Will, Daring the Dawn:

No, as combat cards (such as Skin of Night) cannot be played outside
of combat, which is when the damage dealt by such cards occurs.

Dawn Operation/Weather Control:

Sure.

>I am expecting a "yes" answer, but if so, doesn't that make a daring the dawn/skin of night combo
>entirely unblockable?

Moot.

Messages.Author: Randi S. Herdman
Messages.Body:
Okay, I've been poking around trying to find a definitive answer but I can't.

Can non-preventable aggravated damage (i.e., dawn operation with weather control, force of will,
or daring the dawn) be changed to regular damage using skin of night?

entirely unblockable?

*nods* Which is why the Dawn Op/Skin of Night/Weather Control combo is really

Ulugh. =) Otherwise it's roughly the same. =) I don't normally
like using big-cap vampires either, but it seems pretty tough to get
all the skills you need with at least a COUPLE at superior without
going much above 6. And if you're going to go much above six, you

Doesn't go off very often, requiring six cards. But it's so fun,
especially if they have other vampires who COULD block the
graverobbing action... knowing that they will probably lose -that- one
to torpor as well =)

> I don't know what you've been smoking, but that is simply not true.
> The new errata states "your prey" not "the prey of the person
> controlling this vampire".

Justin is correct.

"You" refers to the controller of the card, as always.

Since Return to Innocence is a minion card, if the controller of the minion
it is on changes, it becomes controlled by the new controller of the minion
it is on.

"Your prey" means "the prey of the controller of this card" which is in this
case "the prey of the controller of this vampire" (barring any unusual
change-controller effects like Succubus Club).

--

You are holding a fire hose, spraying water on a house fire to put it
out. You have begun an effect that targets a house, one that does not
resolve instantaneously. I walk up to you and turn you around so that
you are now spraying water on the house across the street. Does this
matter in the resolution of the effect (ie, do you still successfully
put out the fire) ??

Of course it matters, and that's EXACTLY how the average person will
interpret the card text. If you stop something before it's done
happening, it obviously changes what happens.

RTR 27-OCT-95:
4) If you gain control of a card, you get control of any cards played on it
except for master cards. Note that this is very different from similar
situations in Magic.

Example: You take control of your opponent's Ozmo, who is equipped with a
Laptop and has a Master Discipline card for Protean. You could control the
Laptop, but not the Protean.

> So if you took control of someone's
> Angel with a .44 and they were ousted, the .44 would be gone.

No. You would control both Angel and the .44, so they would both
remain.

> By LSJ's statement, a skill card on a stolen vampire is controlled by whom?

The Methuselah who played it.

> I always thought that control was maintained by whoever played the card
> unless explicit card text changed things.

That's true for Master cards.
Minion cards (non-Master library cards) are controlled by the
controller of the minion (barring explict card text, of course).

it
> > except for master cards. Note that this is very different from similar
> > situations in Magic.
>
> > > I always thought that control was maintained by whoever played the card
> > > unless explicit card text changed things.
> >
> > That's true for Master cards.
> > Minion cards (non-Master library cards) are controlled by the
> > controller of the minion (barring explict card text, of course).
>
> Why the inconsistency as this is obviously a ruling rather than something
> that is in the rulebook? What would be the adverse effects of making
> both minion and master cards the same in "change of controller" situations?

The current system is the most logical/sensical.

You expect minions to "control" weapons, retainers, etc. they have.
Change the controller of the minion, then the controller of those
minion cards on that minion changes as well.

While Master cards "on" minions are not generally "controlled" by the
minion. Often they're not even controlled by the controller of the
minion in common usage (Fame, Haven Uncovered, etc.). It wouldn't
make sense to have the controller of these master cards somehow
linked to the controller of the minion they are on when the control
of the minion changes.

That's the entirety of the explanation.

In article <75n9dt$gmh$1...@nnrp1.dejanews.com>, mboh...@shout.net writes

>> That's true for Master cards.
>> Minion cards (non-Master library cards) are controlled by the
>> controller of the minion (barring explict card text, of course).
>
>Why the inconsistency as this is obviously a ruling rather than something
>that is in the rulebook? What would be the adverse effects of making
>both minion and master cards the same in "change of controller" situations?

Well, if you want Master cards to be controlled by whoever they're on,
look at the Master cards that you put on other vampires. e.g. I put a
Haven Uncovered cross-table and never get the opportunity to defend it
from a burn action because that's directed at the controller, which
would be that vampire's Methuselah - so only his predator and prey get
the opportunity.

Also, it provides the only current method of getting rid of some cards.
Gangrel Atavism, say, cannot be got rid of except by ousting its
controller (since cards you control go with you when you are ousted, but
not cards that have changed control). There are a few cards like this
that would be adversely affected if you couldn't get rid of them because
you controlled them.

Mike Bohlmann wrote:
> > That's true for Master cards.
> > Minion cards (non-Master library cards) are controlled by the
> > controller of the minion (barring explict card text, of course).
>
> Why the inconsistency as this is obviously a ruling rather than something
> that is in the rulebook? What would be the adverse effects of making
> both minion and master cards the same in "change of controller" situations?

Mike, I think a case may be made that any minion card on a vampire (retainers,
equipment, Pulse of Canille, etc.) is owned by the vampire and that anyone
who controls the vampire controls those kind of cards.

Master cards are owned by the "Master" that played them. Which means that
unless somebody specifically takes control of them (like stealing a location)
they are still controlled by the originating player.

That's how it makes sense to me.
